hints: Notice you are given equal masses but different Mr values, so start by thinking in moles to see which reactant will run out first.
Calculate moles of each reactant using n = m / Mr, so 10.0 / 138.0 for the acid and 10.0 / 102.0 for the anhydride.
Use the 1:1 ratio in the equation to take the smaller moles value forward, then convert it back to mass of aspirin with m = n x 180.0.
walkthrough:
**Convert both reactant masses to moles**

Think in moles, not grams, because the equation links particles in a 1:1 ratio. Use the friendly rule moles = mass divided by Mr.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r}$$

**Find the limiting reactant**

For 2-hydroxybenzoic acid:
$$n(\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_3) = \frac{10.0}{138.0} = 0.0725 \text{ mol}$$
For ethanoic anhydride:
$$n(\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_3) = \frac{10.0}{102.0} = 0.0980 \text{ mol}$$
The equation is 1:1, so the acid gives fewer moles and runs out first. It is limiting, the anhydride is in excess.

**Calculate maximum mass of aspirin**

One mole of limiting acid makes one mole of aspirin, so:
$$n(\text{C}_9\text{H}_8\text{O}_4) = 0.0725 \text{ mol}$$
Now convert back to mass:
$$m = n \times M_r = 0.0725 \times 180.0 = 13.0 \text{ g (to 3 s.f.)}$$
That is the maximum possible, assuming complete reaction with no losses.

options.A: Incorrect. About 5.7 g comes from adding the two Mr values together, as if 10.0 / (138.0 + 102.0) gives the moles. You must calculate moles for each reactant separately, the reaction does not use a combined Mr.
options.B: Incorrect. 10.0 g assumes mass of product equals mass of one reactant. Mass is not conserved for one product alone because a second product, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$, is also formed, and Mr values are all different.
options.C: Correct. The acid is limiting with 0.0725 mol, so it can make at most 0.0725 mol of aspirin. Multiplying by 180.0 gives about 13.0 g, which is less than the 17.6 g the excess anhydride could theoretically make.
options.D: Incorrect. 17.6 g is what you get if you wrongly use the excess reactant: (10.0 / 102.0) x 180.0. The anhydride has more moles, but the reaction stops when the 2-hydroxybenzoic acid runs out, so this mass can never be reached.
